canonical_stem: What bounds how long or how much work this operation can perform?

specializations.specialized_stem: What bounds how long or how much work this tool invocation can perform?
What bounds how long or how much work this retrieval request can perform?
What bounds how long or how much work this agent execution can perform?
What bounds how long or how much work this inference request can perform?
What bounds how long or how much work this remote call can perform?
What bounds how long or how much work this background job can perform?

notes: Atomic operation nouns. Overlapping agentic + tool_using_agent + retrieval_system + rag matches multiple specializations; match_policy is unresolved.

canonical_stem: What happens when a primary dependency is unavailable?

specializations.specialized_stem: What happens when a primary model endpoint is unavailable?
What happens when a primary retrieval index is unavailable?
What happens when a primary memory store is unavailable?
What happens when a primary tool is unavailable?
What happens when a primary remote dependency is unavailable?
What happens when a primary upstream service is unavailable?

notes: service_to_service + external_dependency also matches the remote-dependency binding.

canonical_stem: What keeps generated output tied to retrieved or allowed evidence?

specializations.specialized_stem: What keeps generated output tied to retrieved documents?
What keeps generated output tied to retrieved evidence?
What keeps generated output tied to session memory?
What keeps generated output tied to tool output?

notes: retrieval_system alone is NOT_APPLICABLE; llm must be present. rag implies both.

canonical_stem: What limits what this principal or tool is allowed to do?

specializations.specialized_stem: What limits what this human caller is allowed to do?
What limits what this tool is allowed to do?
What limits what this calling service is allowed to do?
What limits what this caller is allowed to do on this public API?
What limits what this external caller is allowed to do?
What limits what this human caller is allowed to do on this internet-facing API?

notes: internet_facing + human_user also matches the human-caller binding.

canonical_stem: How is the caller identified before it is authorized?

specializations.specialized_stem: How is the human caller identified before it is authorized?
How is the calling service identified before it is authorized?
How is the external caller identified before it is authorized?
How is the human caller identified on this internet-facing API before it is authorized?
How is the calling service identified before it is authorized?

notes: Does not name OIDC, mTLS, or other mechanisms.

canonical_stem: What telemetry exists to inspect this operation?

specializations.specialized_stem: What telemetry exists to inspect this service request?
What telemetry exists to inspect this agent execution?
What telemetry exists to inspect this RAG request?
What telemetry exists to inspect this training run?
What telemetry exists to inspect this background job?
What telemetry exists to inspect this on-device run?
What telemetry exists to inspect this inference request?

notes: rag + backend_service matches both the RAG-request and service-request bindings.

canonical_stem: Which actions require a human to approve before they execute?

specializations.specialized_stem: Which gated actions require a human to approve before they execute?
Which tool invocations require a human to approve before they execute?
Which agent actions require a human to approve before they execute?

notes: when always includes human_in_the_loop. HITL + tools + agentic matches all three.

specializations.specialized_stem: How is RAG retrieval relevance evaluated?
How is index retrieval relevance evaluated?

notes: rag implies retrieval_system, so rag-present matches both RAG and index bindings. No nDCG or recall@k. Review dropped s03: backend_service did not discriminate a distinct noun.

canonical_stem: How is a behavior change rolled out gradually rather than all at once?

specializations.specialized_stem: How is a shipped change rolled out gradually rather than all at once?
How is a prompt change rolled out gradually rather than all at once?
How is a model change rolled out gradually rather than all at once?
How is a service change rolled out gradually rather than all at once?
How is a shipped change rolled out gradually rather than all at once?

notes: when always includes ships_behavior_change. No canary, blue-green, or kubernetes.

canonical_stem: How is it evaluated that the agent selected the right tool for the task?

specializations.specialized_stem: How is it evaluated that the agent selected the right tool for the task?
How is it evaluated that the agent selected the right computer-use tool for the task?

notes: computer_use implies tool_using_agent, so both the tool and computer-use-tool bindings match. Review dropped s03: implied traits were not a narrower when.

canonical_stem: How are datasets, models, and prompts stored so a run can be reproduced without copying blobs into git?

specializations.specialized_stem: How are prompts stored so a run can be reproduced without copying blobs into git?
How are models stored so a run can be reproduced without copying blobs into git?
How are datasets stored so a run can be reproduced without copying blobs into git?

notes: prompt_managed + model_artifact matches both prompt and model bindings. Narrowing the canonical list is a binding choice, not a new job.

canonical_stem: What metering exists so spend on tokens, inference, or agents can be seen?

specializations.specialized_stem: What metering exists so spend on tokens can be seen?
What metering exists so spend on inference can be seen?
What metering exists so spend on agents can be seen?
What metering exists so spend on training can be seen?

notes: rag implies llm, so rag-present matches the tokens binding. Narrowing tokens/inference/agents is a binding choice.
